claim: Chromatin boundaries subdivide eukaryotic chromosomes into functionally autonomous domains of genetic activity.
source_text: Chromatin boundaries subdivide eukaryotic chromosomes into functionally autonomous domains of genetic activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established concept in chromatin biology supported by the citation (Gaszner and Felsenfeld, 2006) that follows in the text.

claim: Boundaries shield genes and/or regulatory elements within a domain from adventitious interactions with regulatory elements/genes in nearby domains.
source_text: This subdivision insulates genes and/or regulatory elements within a domain from promiscuous interactions with nearby domains.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the established function of chromatin boundaries, supported by scientific consensus and citations in the introduction.

claim: Elba is a novel developmentally restricted boundary factor.
source_text: Here we report the isolation and characterization of a novel developmentally restricted boundary factor, Elba.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding of the manuscript supported by experimental data presented throughout the results section.

claim: Elba is a hetero-tripartite protein complex that requires all three proteins for DNA binding and insulator activity.
source_text: We show that Elba is an unusual hetero-tripartite protein complex that requires all three proteins for DNA binding and insulator activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding supported by in vitro reconstitution experiments and functional assays shown in Figures 4-6.

claim: Boundary elements can block enhancer-promoter interactions (enhancer-blocking or insulator activity).
source_text: The specific functions that can be ascribed to most boundary elements include an enhancer-blocking or insulator activity
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations (Holdridge and Dorsett, 1991; Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993).

claim: Boundary elements can block silencer activity (silencer-blocking or barrier activity).
source_text: a silencer-blocking or barrier activity
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993; Burgess–Beusse et al., 2002).

claim: Boundary elements can bring distant chromosomal DNA segments in close proximity when combined in specific pairwise combinations.
source_text: when combined in specific pairwise combinations an ability to bring distant chromosomal DNA segments in close proximity
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Cai and Shen, 2001; Muravyova et al., 2001).

claim: In S. pombe, boundaries help restrict and maintain the heterochromatin state of the silenced mating type locus.
source_text: In the yeast S. pombe, boundaries help restrict and maintain the heterochromatin state of the silenced mating type locus
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Noma et al., 2001).

claim: In Drosophila, boundary elements play a critical role in the Bithorax complex (BX-C) in ensuring proper specification of segmental identity.
source_text: In Drosophila, boundary elements play a critical role in the Bithorax complex (BX-C), helping to ensure that the three BX-C homeotic genes properly specify segmental identity
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Maeda and Karch, 2006).

claim: In vertebrates, boundaries have been implicated in controlling expression of neuronal Protocadherin-alpha isoforms and in regulating immunoglobulin gene recombination and expression.
source_text: In vertebrates, boundaries have been implicated in controlling the expression of mRNAs encoding different neuronal Protocadherin-alpha isoforms and in regulating recombination and expression of immunoglobulin light and heavy chain genes
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Guo et al., 2011; Ribeiro de Almeida et al., 2011; Monahan et al., 2012).

claim: The first identified boundaries were able to block regulatory interactions irrespective of cell type or developmental stage.
source_text: The first boundaries identified were able to block adventitious regulatory interactions irrespective of cell type or developmental stage
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Gyurkovics et al., 1990; Holdridge and Dorsett, 1991; Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993).

claim: Boundary proteins like Su(Hw), BEAF, Zw5, GAGA factor and CTCF are ubiquitously expressed and functional in all cell types.
source_text: Moreover, the proteins conferring insulating activity in flies and vertebrates like Su(Hw), BEAF, Zw5, GAGA factor and CTCF are ubiquitously expressed and seemingly functional in all cell types.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the expression patterns of known boundary proteins.

claim: The regulatory domain landscape of eukaryotic chromosomes is more dynamic than previously thought and can be redefined during development, differentiation, and disease progression.
source_text: However recent studies argue that the domain landscape is more dynamic than previously imagined and that genes can be differentially regulated during normal development and differentiation and in the progression of disease states like cancer by redefining their domain organization
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Bell and Felsenfeld, 2000; Witcher and Emerson, 2009; Gomes and Espinosa, 2010).

claim: Regulation of the imprinted Igf2 and H19 genes depends on parent-of-origin differences in DNA methylation pattern and CTCF-dependent boundary element activity.
source_text: For example, regulation of the imprinted Igf2 and H19 genes pivots on parent of origin differences in the DNA methylation pattern and consequently the activity of a CTCF-dependent boundary element upstream of the H19 gene
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Bell and Felsenfeld, 2000; Hark et al., 2000).

claim: The Fab-7 boundary can block the action of enhancers/silencers at all stages of development, apparently irrespective of tissue or cell type.
source_text: Both in the context of BX-C and in transgene assays, the Fab-7 boundary can block the action of enhancers/silencers at all stages of development, apparently irrespective of tissue or cell type
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Galloni et al., 1993; Hagstrom et al., 1996; Mihaly et al., 1997; Schweinsberg et al., 2004).

claim: The Fab-7 boundary spans a sequence of 1.2 kb and consists of two prominent and one minor chromatin-specific nuclease hypersensitive regions.
source_text: The Fab-7 boundary spans a sequence of 1.2 kb and consists of two prominent and one minor (*) chromatin specific nuclease hypersensitive regions
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the structure of Fab-7.

claim: pHS1 is a 236-bp fragment from the proximal side of HS1 which has enhancer-blocking activity only in early embryos.
source_text: pHS1 is a 236-bp fragment from the proximal side of HS1 which has enhancer-blocking activity only in early embryos
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation (Schweinsberg and Schedl, 2004) and experimental data.

claim: The enhancer-blocking activity of pHS1 in early embryos depends upon an 8-bp sequence, CCAATAAG, called Elba.
source_text: In addition to the GAGA sites, the enhancer-blocking activity of pHS1 in early embryos also depends upon an 8-bp sequence, CCAATAAG, called Elba (Early boundary activity).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by previous work (Aoki et al., 2008) and experimental data showing mutations in this sequence compromise blocking activity.

claim: Elba factor binding is detected in 0–6 hr nuclear extracts, but is absent in 6–12 hr nuclear extracts.
source_text: Elba factor binding is detected in 0–6 hr nuclear extracts, but it is absent in 6–12 hr (and 6–18 hr) nuclear extracts
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by EMSA experiments from previous work (Aoki et al., 2008).

claim: Mutations in the Elba recognition sequence that disrupt Elba binding in nuclear extracts compromise pHS1 insulator activity in vivo.
source_text: We found that mutations in the recognition sequence that disrupt Elba binding in nuclear extracts compromise pHS1 insulator activity in vivo.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by previous work (Aoki et al., 2008) showing functional consequences of mutations.

claim: Multimerizing the Elba recognition sequence is sufficient to confer early insulating activity.
source_text: Conversely, multimerizing the Elba recognition sequence is sufficient to confer early insulating activity
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by previous work (Aoki et al., 2008) and transgene assays.

claim: The Elba boundary factor is a hetero-tripartite protein complex consisting of Elba1, Elba2, and Elba3.
source_text: Using this purification strategy, we show that the Elba boundary factor is an unusual hetero-tripartite protein complex.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding supported by mass spectrometry data in Table 1 and reconstitution experiments in Figures 4-6.

claim: Elba1 and Elba2 share a conserved C-terminal 'BEN domain'.
source_text: Two of the proteins, Elba1 and Elba2, share a conserved C-terminal 'BEN domain'
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 3C and bioinformatics analysis.

claim: Elba3 has no obvious conserved protein domains.
source_text: The third protein, Elba3, has no obvious conserved protein domains
evidence_reasoning: This is based on sequence analysis and bioinformatics searches.

claim: The elba3 gene is closely linked to elba1.
source_text: but is encoded by a gene that is closely linked to Elba1
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by genomic location data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: All three Elba proteins are required to reconstitute DNA binding activity in vitro.
source_text: All three Elba proteins are required to reconstitute DNA binding activity in vitro.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by in vitro reconstitution experiments shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: DNA binding by the Elba complex depends upon the BEN domains in Elba1 and Elba2.
source_text: DNA binding depends upon the BEN domains in Elba1 and Elba2
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by deletion experiments shown in Figure 5B where removal of BEN domains eliminates DNA binding.

claim: Elba3 mediates the assembly of an active Elba complex by interacting with the N-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2.
source_text: while Elba3 mediates the assembly of an active Elba complex by interacting with the N-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from experiments showing that GST can substitute for Elba3 when fused to N-termini of Elba1 and Elba2 (Figure 6), and that C-terminal fragments don't interact with Elba3.

claim: All three Elba proteins are present in the Elba complex detected in 0–6 hr nuclear extracts.
source_text: All three Elba proteins are present in the Elba complex detected in 0–6 hr nuclear extracts
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by antibody supershift experiments shown in Figure 4D where antibodies against each protein supershift the Elba-DNA complex.

claim: All three Elba proteins are required for chromatin domain boundary function in vivo.
source_text: and all three are required for chromatin domain boundary function in vivo.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 9 where depletion of any of the three proteins compromises boundary activity.

claim: elba1 and elba3 are 'mid-blastula transition' genes.
source_text: Finally, because elba1 and elba3 are 'mid-blastula transition' genes
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by Northern blot data in Figure 7 and citation (Singer and Lengyel, 1997) for elba1/Bsg25A.

claim: Elba only binds to its target sequences in Fab-7 and confers insulator activity during early embryogenesis.
source_text: Elba only binds to its' target sequences in Fab-7 and confers insulator activity during early embryogenesis.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by ChIP experiments in Figure 8 showing Elba binding in early but not late embryos, and functional assays showing early-specific activity.

claim: A cross-affinity purification strategy substantially reduces non-specific proteins and increases differences in Elba yield between wild type and mutant affinity beads.
source_text: To reduce the number of remaining non-specific binding proteins and increase the differences in Elba yield between WT and M affinity beads, we devised the cross affinity purification scheme
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by comparing the results of single vs. cross-affinity purification experiments described in the text and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Three proteins (CG12205/Elba1, CG15634/Elba3, and CG9883/Elba2) were substantially enriched in the MSW1 fraction compared to all other proteins.
source_text: while there were still 176 unique proteins in the MSW1 fraction, three of these were substantially enriched compared to all others (Table 1). Each had 16 or more confirmed peptides with high spectral counts and their sequence coverage was over 25%.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Table 1.

claim: Elba1 is encoded by a previously described mid-blastula transition gene, Bsg25A, of unknown function.
source_text: One protein, Elba1: CG12205, is encoded by a previously described mid-blastula transition gene, Bsg25A, of unknown function
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Singer and Lengyel, 1997).

claim: Elba2 and Elba3 are products of uncharacterized genes.
source_text: while the other two, Elba2: CG9883 and Elba3: CG15634, are products of uncharacterized genes.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the state of knowledge at the time of the study.

claim: All three Elba proteins are approximately 40 kDa in size.
source_text: First, all three are ∼40 kDa, which is close in size to the protein species in nuclear extracts that is UV cross-linked to probes containing the Elba sequence
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by mass spectrometry data (Table 1) and previous UV cross-linking experiments (Aoki et al., 2008).

claim: The C-terminal ∼130 amino acids of Elba1 and Elba2 show extensive sequence similarities.
source_text: Second, the C-terminal ∼130 amino acids of Elba1 and Elba2 show extensive sequence similarities
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by sequence alignment shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The BEN domain is a conserved ∼90 amino acid domain that has been implicated in protein:protein interactions and transcriptional regulation.
source_text: Moreover, included within this region of similarity is a conserved ∼90 amino acids BEN domain (Figure 3B) that has been implicated in protein:protein interactions and transcriptional regulation
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Cha et al., 1997; Mackler et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2006; Korutla et al., 2009; Duan et al., 2011).

claim: Insensitive (Insv) is a Drosophila protein with a BEN domain that functions in neurogenesis and Notch signaling.
source_text: while the other is Insensitive (Insv) (Figure 3C), which functions in neurogenesis and Notch signaling
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Duan et al., 2011).

claim: The elba2 and Insv transcription units are paired with each other.
source_text: Interestingly, the elba2 and Insv transcription units are paired with each other
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by genomic location data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Elba1 is most closely related to mammalian BEND7.
source_text: Of the mammalian proteins, Elba1 is most closely related to BEND7
evidence_reasoning: This is based on sequence similarity analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Elba2 is most closely related to mammalian BEND6.
source_text: while Elba2 is most closely related to BEND6
evidence_reasoning: This is based on sequence similarity analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The BEN domain of Insv is most closely related to BEN9/hNAC2 and BEND8/hNAC1.
source_text: The BEN domain of Insv is most closely related to BEN9/hNAC2 and BEND8/hNAC1.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on sequence similarity analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The elba3 transcription unit is located next to elba1.
source_text: Finally, though Elba3 differs from Elba1 and Elba2 in that it has no distinctive domains, its transcription unit is located next to elba1
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by genomic location data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: None of the three Elba proteins individually has DNA binding activity when synthesized by in vitro translation.
source_text: None of the three proteins had DNA binding activity on their own
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by EMSA experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Mixing all three in vitro translated Elba proteins generates a shift with the same mobility as the Elba shift in nuclear extracts.
source_text: However, when all three proteins were mixed, we observed a shift with the same mobility as the Elba shift in nuclear extracts
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by EMSA experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The sequence specificity of reconstituted Elba is the same as nuclear extract Elba.
source_text: Figure 4C shows that sequence specificity of reconstituted Elba is the same as nuclear extract Elba.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by competition EMSA experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: All six immune sera against the three Elba proteins give an Elba supershift, while pre-immune sera do not.
source_text: Figure 4D shows that all six immune sera give an Elba supershift, while the Elba shift is unchanged by the corresponding pre-immune sera.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by antibody supershift experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The Elba antibodies do not supershift probes from elsewhere in Fab-7 that are recognized by factors present in 6–12 hr but not 0–6 hr nuclear extracts.
source_text: As an additional control for specificity we tested whether these sera would supershift probes from elsewhere in Fab-7 that are recognized by factors which are present in 6–12 hr but not 0–6 hr nuclear extracts. We found that they did not.
evidence_reasoning: This is a control experiment demonstrating antibody specificity.

claim: Mixing bacterially expressed N-terminal GST fusions of Elba1 and Elba2 in the absence of Elba3 produces very weak but detectable DNA binding activity.
source_text: In preliminary experiments, we found very weak, but detectable DNA binding activity when we mixed bacterially expressed N-terminal GST (Glutahione-S-transferase) fusions of the two BEN domain proteins, Elba1 and Elba2, in the absence of Elba3.
evidence_reasoning: This is an experimental observation that led to further investigation.

claim: GST forms stable dimers.
source_text: Since GST is known to form stable dimers
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the biochemical properties of GST.

claim: Deleting the BEN domain from Elba1 or Elba2 eliminates DNA binding activity when the three full-length proteins are mixed.
source_text: Figure 5B shows that mixing the three full-length proteins (which have N-terminal FLAG tags as do all of the other proteins in Figure 5A) generates the Elba shift, while the shift is eliminated whenever a BEN domain deletion is used instead for reconstitution.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by EMSA experiments with deletion mutants shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Co-translating mRNAs encoding GST-Elba1F and GST-Elba2F fusions generates DNA binding activity without Elba3.
source_text: To maximize the formation of heterodimers, we co-translated mRNAs encoding the GST-Elba1F and GST-Elba2F fusions and assayed for DNA binding activity. As shown in lane 6 of [Figure 6A], the GST-Elba1:GST-Elba2 heterodimer has DNA binding activity comparable to the native hetero-tripartite complex
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by EMSA experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The GST-Elba1C:GST-Elba2C heterodimer (containing only C-terminal domains) has DNA binding activity comparable to the native hetero-tripartite complex.
source_text: Like the full-length GST fusions, the GST-ElbaC homodimers have no detectable DNA binding activity on their own (Figure 6A, lanes 14 and 15), while a very prominent shift is generated when the RNAs encoding GST-Elba1C and GST-Elba2C are co-translated (lane 13).
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by EMSA experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The GST-Elba1C:GST-Elba2C heterodimer exhibits similar sequence specificity to the native hetero-tripartite Elba complex.
source_text: In addition to having roughly equivalent activity to the 'native' hetero-tripartite Elba complex generated by the three full length Elba proteins, the GST-Elba1C:GST-Elba2C heterodimer exhibits a similar sequence specificity
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by competition EMSA experiments shown in Figures 4C and 6C.

claim: The addition of Elba3 to the two ElbaC proteins (without GST) does not reconstitute full DNA binding activity.
source_text: Most importantly, the addition of Elba3 to the two ElbaC proteins (without the GST moiety) does not reconstitute full DNA binding activity (Figure 6D, lane 7).
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by EMSA experiments shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Elba3 orchestrates the formation of the hetero-tripartite complex by interacting with sequences in the N-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2.
source_text: This finding suggests that Elba3 orchestrates the formation of the hetero-tripartite complex by interacting with sequences in the N-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that C-terminal fragments don't interact with Elba3 while full-length proteins do.

claim: The shift generated by the GST-Elba1C:GST-Elba2C heterodimer is not supershifted by the addition of Elba3.
source_text: Consistent with this idea, the shift generated by the active GST-Elba1C:GST-Elba2C heterodimer differs from the full-length heterodimer in that it is not supershifted by the addition of Elba3 (Figure 6A, lane 12).
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by EMSA experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The mixture of Elba1C and Elba2C proteins (lacking GST) gives a faint shift that can be detected in long exposures.
source_text: A second potentially interesting difference is that the mixture of Elba1C and Elba2C proteins (lacking GST) gives a faint shift that can be detected in long (Figure 6D, lane 8 filled arrowhead) but not short (Figure 6A, lane 16) exposures.
evidence_reasoning: This is an experimental observation from EMSA experiments shown in Figures 6A and 6D.

claim: There are weakly active hetero-dimerization motifs in the C-terminal halves of Elba1 and Elba2 that become more accessible when the N-terminus is removed.
source_text: Although further studies will be required, it would appear that there are weakly active hetero-dimerization motifs in the C-terminal halves of Elba1 and Elba2 that become more readily accessible when the N-terminus of the two proteins is removed.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative interpretation of the weak DNA binding activity observed with C-terminal fragments lacking GST.

claim: Neither the N- nor C-terminal halves of Elba3 supported complex formation when mixed with the two other Elba proteins.
source_text: As for the N- and C-terminal halves of Elba3, neither supported complex formation when mixed with the two other Elba proteins (not shown)
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: Neither the N- nor C-terminal halves of Elba3 supershift the shift generated by the GST-Elba1F:GST-Elba2F dimer.
source_text: nor did they supershift the shift generated by the GST-Elba1F:GST-Elba2F dimer (see Figure 6E).
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by EMSA experiments shown in Figure 6E.

claim: elba1 mRNA is present at high levels in 2–4 hr and 4–6 hr embryos and then largely disappears during the remainder of embryogenesis.
source_text: As shown in Figure 7, elba1 mRNA is present at high levels in 2–4 hr and 4–6 hr embryos and then largely disappears during the remainder of embryogenesis.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by Northern blot experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: elba3 mRNA has a similar temporal expression pattern to elba1.
source_text: elba3 mRNA has a similar temporal expression pattern.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by Northern blot experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: elba2 mRNA is maternally deposited and present throughout embryogenesis.
source_text: In contrast, elba2 mRNA is maternally deposited and present throughout embryogenesis.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by Northern blot experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: insv mRNA is maternally deposited and present throughout embryogenesis.
source_text: Like elba2, insv mRNA is maternally deposited and present throughout embryogenesis.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by Northern blot experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: Elba1 and Elba2 are associated with Fab-7 in 2–5 hr embryos but not in 9–12 hr embryos.
source_text: As shown in Figure 8A,B, both Elba1 and Elba2 are associated with Fab-7 in 2–5 hr embryos, but not in 9–12 hr embryos.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by ChIP experiments shown in Figure 8A,B.

claim: Elba1 and Elba2 are not associated with control sequences from the twine and Sex-lethal genes in either early or late embryos.
source_text: In contrast, neither protein is associated with control sequences from the twine and Sex-lethal genes in either early or late embryos.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by ChIP experiments shown in Figure 8A,B as a specificity control.

claim: Injection of dsRNA specific for elba1, elba2, or elba3 compromises the insulating activity of pHS1×4 in early embryos.
source_text: In contrast to the buffer control, injection of dsRNA specific for elba1, elba2 or elba3 compromised the insulating activity of pHS1×4.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by RNAi injection experiments shown in Figure 9.

claim: Injection of dsRNA specific for insv does not affect the insulating activity of pHS1×4.
source_text: On the other hand, injection of dsRNA specific for insv had no effect.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by RNAi injection experiments shown in Figure 9 as a specificity control.

claim: The constitutive insulator activity of Fab-7 is generated by sub-elements whose activity is developmentally restricted.
source_text: The constitutive insulator activity of the Fab-7 boundary is generated by a series of functionally redundant sub-elements whose activity is developmentally restricted.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion supported by the current work and previous studies cited in the introduction.

claim: Elba confers the insulator activity of pHS1 in early embryos.
source_text: Here we report the identification and characterization of a factor, Elba, which confers the insulator activity of one of these sub-elements in early embryos.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary conclusion supported by multiple lines of evidence including binding assays, ChIP, and functional tests.

claim: The BEN domain has been implicated in protein:protein interactions and transcriptional regulation.
source_text: The BEN domain is found in insect and vertebrate nuclear proteins and has been implicated in protein:protein interactions and transcriptional regulation
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Abhiman et al., 2008).

claim: DNA binding by the Elba complex is mediated by the C-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2.
source_text: Our functional studies indicate that DNA binding is mediated by the C-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experiments with C-terminal fragments shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Elba1 and Elba2 must be linked in a 'heterodimer' to form a DNA binding 'pocket' that recognizes the asymmetric Elba sequence.
source_text: however, in order to form a DNA binding 'pocket' that recognizes the asymmetric Elba sequence, CCAATAAG, Elba1 and Elba2 must be linked in a 'heterodimer'
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from experiments showing that homodimers don't bind DNA while heterodimers do.

claim: In the tripartite Elba complex, Elba3 brings Elba1 and Elba2 together by interacting with sequences in the N-terminal half of the two proteins.
source_text: In the tripartite Elba complex, this seems to be the role of Elba3. It brings Elba1 and Elba2 together by interacting with sequences in the N-terminal half of the two proteins.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from experiments showing that GST can substitute for Elba3 when fused to N-termini, and that C-terminal fragments don't interact with Elba3.

claim: It is possible to circumvent the requirement for Elba3 by fusing GST to the N-terminus of full length Elba1 and Elba2.
source_text: First, it is possible to circumvent the requirement for Elba3 by fusing a heterologous dimerization domain, in this case GST, to the N-terminus of full length Elba1 and Elba2.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: GST-Elba1F and GST-Elba2F can still interact with Elba3 as evidenced by supershifting.
source_text: On the other hand, they can still interact with Elba3 as the shift generated by the two proteins can be supershifted by the addition of Elba3.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The Elba DNA binding pocket is likely formed by a GST-Elba1C:GST-Elba2C dimer rather than by some other more complicated combination.
source_text: Since GST is known to dimerize, but not form higher order complexes, this would argue that the Elba DNA binding pocket is likely formed by a GST-Elba1C:GST-Elba2C dimer rather than by some other more complicated combination of the two proteins.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the properties of GST and the DNA binding activity of the GST-ElbaC heterodimer.

claim: The presence of functionally redundant elements in full length Fab-7 precludes direct demonstration that a single factor like Elba is needed for Fab-7 insulating activity.
source_text: As would be the case for many other boundaries, the presence of functionally redundant elements in the full length Fab-7 precludes a direct demonstration that a single factor like Elba is needed for Fab-7 insulating activity either in the context of BX-C or in transgenes assays.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the experimental limitations imposed by functional redundancy.

claim: The insulating activity of pHS1 in early embryos is compromised when the Elba recognition sequence is mutated.
source_text: To begin with, previous studies showed that the insulating activity of the 236-bp pHS1 Fab-7 sub-element in early embryos is compromised when the Elba recognition sequence is mutated.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by previous work (Aoki et al., 2008).

claim: When multimerized, the Elba sequence is sufficient on its own to confer insulating activity.
source_text: Moreover, when multimerized, the Elba sequence is sufficient on its own to confer insulating activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by previous work (Aoki et al., 2008) and experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: RNAi knockdowns of all three Elba proteins compromise the insulating activity of both pHS1×4 and the Elba multimer.
source_text: For all three Elba proteins, RNAi knockdowns compromises the insulating activity of both pHS1×4 and the Elba multimer.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by RNAi injection experiments shown in Figure 9 and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: Knockdowns of the closely related BEN domain protein Insv have no effect on insulating activity.
source_text: In contrast, knockdowns of the closely related BEN domain protein, Insv, have no effect.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by RNAi injection experiments shown in Figure 9 as a specificity control.

claim: The insulating activity of the Elba factor/Elba sequence is developmentally restricted because Elba1 and Elba3 are encoded by mid-blastula transition genes.
source_text: Our findings would also explain why the insulating activity of the Elba factor/Elba sequence is developmentally restricted. Two of the three Elba proteins, Elba1 and Elba3, are encoded by genes that are active during the mid-blastula transition, but not later in development.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the temporal expression patterns shown in Figure 7 and the requirement for all three proteins.

claim: Elba insulating activity would be expected to peak during the blastoderm/early gastrula stage when high levels of elba1 and elba3 mRNA are expressed.
source_text: Since the hetero-tripartite complex is required to reconstitute DNA binding activity, Elba insulating activity would be expected to peak during the blastoderm/early gastrula stage when high levels of elba1 and elba3 mRNA are expressed.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference from the requirement for all three proteins and the expression patterns.

claim: Elba insulating activity should gradually dissipate after transcription of elba1 and elba3 ceases.
source_text: However, it should gradually dissipate after transcription of elba1 and elba3 ceases.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference from the requirement for all three proteins and the cessation of elba1 and elba3 transcription.

claim: There is little Elba DNA binding activity in nuclear extracts of 6–12 hr embryos.
source_text: While we don't know precisely when Elba1 and Elba3 disappear, there is little Elba DNA binding activity in nuclear extracts of 6–12 hr embryos.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by EMSA experiments with staged nuclear extracts.

claim: elba2 is not found associated with Fab-7 in 9–12 hr embryos even though the elba2 gene is expressed throughout development.
source_text: Moreover, even though the elba2 gene is expressed throughout development, it is not found associated with Fab-7 in 9–12 hr embryos.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by ChIP experiments shown in Figure 8.

claim: The requirement for Elba activity evident in RNAi knockdowns reflects a direct role in insulating activity rather than an indirect role.
source_text: Importantly, the results of the EMSA and ChIP experiments provide strong support for the idea that the requirement for Elba activity evident in the RNAi knockdowns reflects a direct role in insulating activity rather than indirect role.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the combination of binding data (EMSA, ChIP) and functional data (RNAi).

claim: Boundaries function in combination (likely pairwise) with other boundaries.
source_text: A plausible explanation comes from the finding that boundaries are not autonomous entities, but rather function in combination (likely pairwise) with other boundaries
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Cai and Shen, 2001; Muravyova et al., 2001).

claim: Some boundary combinations are functional while others are not, as shown by boundary competition and bypass experiments.
source_text: Both boundary competition (Gohl et al., 2011) and boundary bypass experiments (Kyrchanova et al., 2008a; Maksimenko et al., 2008) indicate that some combinations are functional while others are not.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by the cited references.

claim: How different boundary combinations work together depends upon developmental stage and tissue.
source_text: Moreover, how different boundary combinations work together depends upon developmental stage and tissue
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Gohl et al., 2011).

claim: The use of stage-specific factors at Fab-7 could reflect a need to optimize combinations with other nearby BX-C boundaries or the Abdominal-B promoter.
source_text: Thus, the use of stage specific factors at Fab-7 could reflect a need to optimize combinations with other nearby BX-C boundaries or the Abdominal-B promoter
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative reasoning supported by citations (Kyrchanova et al., 2008b, 2011).

claim: When heterologous boundaries replace Fab-7 in BX-C, they are unable to provide bypass activity and their insulating activity can be lost in a stage and tissue specific fashion.
source_text: When heterologous boundaries are used to replace Fab-7 in BX-C, they are unable to provide bypass activity, while their insulating activity can be lost in a stage and tissue specific fashion
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Hogga et al., 2001).

claim: Fab-7 is able to replace Fab-8.
source_text: In contrast, Fab-7 is able to replace Fab-8
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Iampietro et al., 2008).

claim: The boundary activity of Fab-7 in a foreign environment is context dependent and varies during development.
source_text: Likewise, the boundary activity of Fab-7 in a foreign environment is not only context dependent, but also varies during development
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Gohl et al., 2011).

claim: Bypass is observed when Fab-7 is combined with the neighboring boundaries Fab-6 and Fab-8, while bypass interactions with boundaries from elsewhere in BX-C are only weak at best.
source_text: They found that bypass is observed when Fab-7 is combined with the neighboring boundaries Fab-6 and Fab-8, while bypass interactions with boundaries from elsewhere in BX-C are only weak at best.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Kyrchanova et al., 2011).

claim: Boundary bypass is mediated by homologous protein:protein interactions in the cases that have been analyzed most thoroughly.
source_text: Interestingly, in the cases that have been analyzed most thoroughly, boundary bypass is mediated by homologous protein:protein interactions
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Kyrchanova et al., 2008a).

claim: Bypass is observed when multimerized binding sites for the dCTCF boundary factor are paired, but not when dCTCF binding sites are paired with sites for Zw5.
source_text: Thus, bypass is observed when multimerized binding sites for the dCTCF boundary factor are paired, but not when dCTCF binding sites are paired with sites for example Zw5.
evidence_reasoning: This is an example illustrating the specificity of bypass interactions.

claim: Fab-8 utilizes dCTCF.
source_text: Though Fab-8 differs from Fab-7 in that it utilizes dCTCF
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Holohan et al., 2007; Kyrchanova et al., 2011).

claim: EMSA experiments indicate that Fab-7 and Fab-8 have binding sites for several of the same stage specific factors.
source_text: EMSA experiments with 0–6 hr and 6–12 hr nuclear extracts indicate that they also have binding sites for several of the same stage specific factors
evidence_reasoning: This is based on EMSA experiments from previous work (Aoki et al., 2008) and unpublished data.

claim: Fab-7 and Fab-8 have sites for the Elba factor and for two different late (6–12 hr) stage specific factors.
source_text: These include sites for the Elba factor, and sites for two different late (6–12 hr) stage specific factors.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on EMSA experiments from previous work (Aoki et al., 2008) and unpublished data.

claim: Elba2 could function as an insulator in other contexts using different protein partners after Elba1 and Elba3 disappear.
source_text: While Elba2 can't bind to the Elba sequence on its own, it could function as an insulator in other contexts using different protein partners and presumably also recognition sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative reasoning about the potential function of Elba2 in later development.

claim: Insv is a plausible partner for Elba2 in later developmental contexts.
source_text: A plausible partner would be the Notch signaling pathway protein Insv, which is encoded by a tightly linked gene that has a similar expression pattern to elba2.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative reasoning based on genomic linkage and expression patterns.

claim: Insv and its closest mammalian relatives, the NAC proteins, are believed to regulate transcription by acting as co-repressors.
source_text: Insv and its closest mammalian relatives, the NAC proteins (which are thought to function as stem cell pluripotency genes, as well as in cocaine addiction and cancer), are believed to regulate transcription by acting as co-repressors
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Cha et al., 1997; Mackler et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2006; Korutla et al., 2009; Duan et al., 2011).

claim: The BEN domains of Elba1 and Elba2 are essential for DNA binding, suggesting that Insv and mammalian counterparts may be sequence specific DNA binding proteins rather than co-repressors.
source_text: However, since our findings indicate that the BEN domains of Elba1 and Elba2 are essential for DNA binding, it would be reasonable to suppose that Insv as well as the mammalian counterparts are not co-repressors, but are rather sequence specific DNA binding proteins.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative reasoning based on the findings about Elba BEN domains.

claim: CTCF was initially thought to be a transcriptional repressor.
source_text: Interestingly, like members of the BEN domain protein family, CTCF was initially thought to be a transcriptional repressor
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Filippova et al., 1996).

claim: Other members of the BEN family besides the two Elba proteins may function as insulators restricting the action of nearby enhancer elements instead of directly repressing transcription.
source_text: Thus, a seemingly plausible speculation would be that other members of the BEN family besides the two Elba proteins function as insulators restricting the action of nearby enhancer elements instead of directly repressing transcription.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative reasoning based on the findings about Elba and the history of CTCF.

claim: The mammalian BEN domain protein SMAR1 is a component of the nuclear matrix and associates with Matrix Attachment Regions (MARS).
source_text: Potentially supporting this idea is the finding that one of the mammalian BEN domain proteins, SMAR1, is a component of the nuclear matrix and associates with Matrix Attachment Regions (MARS)
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Chattopadhyay et al., 2000).

claim: If other BEN domain proteins function as insulators, CTCF would not be the only vertebrate insulator protein.
source_text: If this were the case, this would mean that CTCF is not the only vertebrate insulator protein.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative reasoning about the implications if BEN domain proteins function as insulators.

claim: Modulating the expression or activity of Elba2, Insv or NAC1 in different tissues or cell types could change the regulatory domain landscapes and alter global patterns of gene expression.
source_text: Also as is case for the Elba complex, modulating the expression or activity of Elba2, Insv or NAC1 in different tissues or cell types could change the regulatory domain landscapes, and potentially alter global patterns of gene expression.
evidence_reasoning: This is speculative reasoning about the potential regulatory implications of BEN domain proteins.
